Subject: RE: Urgent: drop in throughput and 500s impacting inference (18:23 UTC)

Triage summary (engineering):
- Timeline: 18:22 UTC — autoscaler initiated bin-packing; 18:23 UTC — a small percentage of inference workers started returning 500 due to an L2 cache miss path in the new kernel selector.
- Root cause (prelim): regression in kernel selection heuristics combined with an aggressive cache eviction policy we rolled this morning. Under the traffic spike, some KV cache entries were evicted and the fallback code path was causing transient panics on a subset of quantized kernels.
- Impact: ~12 minutes of elevated 5xx and a drop in sustained throughput (throughput cliff).

Immediate mitigations executed:
1) Rolled traffic to a compatible non-quantized runtime variant for the affected model (short-term fallback) — restored normal throughput for 95% of traffic by 18:36 UTC.
2) Increased autoscaler thresholds to avoid thrashing while we review bin-packing settings.
3) Reverted the cache eviction setting flagged in today's config change to its previous value.

Next steps (owned):
- Marissa: produce RCA draft and reproduce steps in staging with kernel selector logging (target: 2028-07-31 11:59 PT).
- David: prepare a patch for the kernel selector and add defensive guard for the quantized fallback (target: 2028-08-03 EOD PT).
- Irene: schedule an exec-level readout for Aster + Redwood leadership and propose customer remediation (credits + post-incident support) (target: 2028-07-31 morning).

Attachments: cpu-metrics-18-23.png (attached), initial logs links in SUP-1234.

— Marissa
VP, Runtime & Reliability

Subject: Aster Health — incident summary, RCA draft, and action cadence

Jamie — thank you again for your patience. Below is the delivery summary and next-steps cadence. A draft RCA is attached (rca-draft.docx).

Summary (concise):
- Incident window: 2028-07-30 18:22–18:36 UTC.
- Impact: transient 500-series errors and ~60% reduction in sustained inference throughput for a subset of requests. No customer data exposure.
- Root cause (final draft): an interaction between a new kernel-selector heuristic and a changed cache-eviction policy caused an unexpected fallback path on quantized kernels; the fallback path lacked a defensive handling for a rare panicking case.
- Immediate outcome: traffic routed to a compatible runtime variant and cache-eviction setting reverted. Service levels restored within ~13 minutes.

Action items and ownership: 
- Marissa Cole: Finalize RCA, add kernel-selector unit tests, and validate fix in staging (target: 2028-07-31 11:59 PT).
- David Kim: Land kernel-selector patch with defensive guard, plus canary rollout plan (target: 2028-08-03 EOD PT).
- Irene Choi: Execute exec readout with Aster leadership, confirm remediation proposal (customer credit + 3 months of priority ops support), and run weekly follow-up cadence until closure (first follow-up: 2028-08-07).
- Jonas Weber: Confirm rollback runbook and owner; ensure CS messaging templates are ready (target: 2028-07-31 12:30 PT).

We will share the final RCA doc and the retrospective notes in the SUP-1234 ticket and on the shared drive link. I've attached the RCA draft and the CPU chart that Jamie sent.

If you prefer a shorter executive note for Aster's CEO and CIO, I can prepare a one-page summary for signatures by EOD.
